notes: Codex CLI is not available in the test sandbox and no real project is mounted. Test runs use a mock `codex` on PATH that returns a fixed critique against a sample ADR in a throwaway git repo. This exercises the full orchestration (arg parsing, correct codex invocation, feedback handoff, assumptions+review list, offer-to-edit) deterministically. It does NOT validate real Codex output quality.

evals.name: happy-path-with-path-arg
evals.expected_output: Skill resolves the file, invokes codex exec with the configured model and xhigh reasoning against the current project (read-only), reads Codex's feedback, then produces a point-by-point list where each Codex finding (with its severity) is paired with Claude's own verdict and reasoning. Ends by offering to apply edits.

evals.name: missing-path-asks-user
evals.expected_output: Skill does not guess a file. It asks the user which file to evaluate and waits, rather than picking one or running Codex against nothing.

evals.name: natural-language-second-opinion
evals.prompt: can you poke holes in my caching design doc? it's at docs/design/redis-caching.md — i want a real second opinion, not just you agreeing with me
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers without the /command syntax, runs Codex against the doc, and returns the assumptions+review list with genuine Claude verdicts (including disagreement where warranted), not a rubber-stamp of Codex.
